|           THE BRAUN -> APPLE VISUAL LINEAGE                          |
|                                                                      |
|  BRAUN (1955-1995)              APPLE (1998-2020s)                   |
|  Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot      Jonathan Ive                         |
|                                                                      |
|  T3 pocket radio (1958)  -->    iPod (2001)                          |
|  Cylindrical, minimal,          Same cylindrical minimalism          |
|  control on face                scroll wheel on face                 |
|                                                                      |
|  SK4 phonograph (1956)   -->    Power Mac G5 (2003)                  |
|  "Snow White's coffin"          Brushed aluminum, flat horizontal    |
|  flat lid, aluminum grid        Same proportional language           |
|                                                                      |
|  L2 speaker (1958)       -->    Mac Pro cylinder (2013)              |
|  Cylindrical speaker            Cylindrical, single aperture top     |
|  simple perforated face                                              |
|                                                                      |
|  ET66 calculator (1977)  -->    iPhone/iPad calculator app (2007)    |
|  Grid layout, flat keys,        Pixel-perfect recreation in pixels   |
|  neutral colors                                                      |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+

ET66 POCKET CALCULATOR (Braun, 1977)
Dietrich Lubs (under Rams)

FEATURES:
  -- Buttons: each function type in distinct color
    Arithmetic ops: same color
    Number keys: neutral
    = key: accented color
  -- Screen: recessed above key area
  -- Overall: perfectly rectangular; rounded corners

iPHONE CALCULATOR APP COMPARISON:
  The original iPhone calculator app (2007):
  -- Pixel-perfect recreation of the ET66 layout
  -- Same button color logic
  -- Same grid proportions
  -- The only difference: screen at top vs bottom

DESIGN PRINCIPLE DEMONSTRATED:
  When the layout logic is correct, it can be reproduced
  across any medium (plastic object -> software pixels)
  and remain recognizable and functional.
